historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-0.2%) diverges enormously from revenue (6.0%) and EPS (19.4%) 5yr CAGRs -- this is NOT organic weakness; it is a near-100%+ earnings payout via buybacks/dividends holding book value flat while the underlying fee/premium business compounds (see inputs.notes). Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor for this ticker, unlike the house default. FCF 3yr CAGR (65.9%) is inflated by a depressed FY2022 base (catastrophe-heavy year, owner FCF $328.5M) and is not used either; revenue 3yr CAGR (7.9%, off a normal base) is the selected anchor, corroborated by FY2026 guidance (Global Lifestyle low-double-digit, blended ~mid-single-to-high-single-digit) and H1-2026 actual revenue growth of +10.3% YoY.

scenario_narratives.base: Global Lifestyle scales recently won mobile/device partnerships into low-double-digit segment growth per FY2026 guidance; Global Housing grows modestly through normal catastrophe/reserve noise; EBITDA margin continues its FY2023-2025 expansion trend toward a mature ~12.2% on operating leverage and AI-enabled claims automation; revenue growth decelerates from ~8.5% to a 3% terminal rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: Partnership wins scale faster and stickier than guided, international Connected Living expansion and vehicle+mobile bundling add a second growth leg, Global Housing avoids major catastrophe years, and margin expands further to ~13.2% as buybacks accelerate.
scenario_narratives.bear: A concentrated carrier/OEM partner is lost or repriced, device-protection attach rates erode secularly as replacement cycles lengthen, Global Housing catastrophe/reserve development worsens beyond the guided headwind, and competitive pricing from Asurion/InsurTechs compresses margin toward 10%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Assurant is legally an insurance holding company but economically a fee/premium-based protection distribution business (Global Lifestyle mobile/device protection and extended service contracts, Global Housing lender-placed and renters insurance) with short-tail claims and a small claims reserve ($2.1B) relative to a large but matched unearned-premium/DAC book ($20.9B/$10.2B) -- not a long-duration investment-float compounder. Owner FCF has been a clean, growing, non-noisy series over FY2022-2025 ($328.5M -> $1,498.9M) tracking revenue and margin expansion, so this model uses the standard owner-FCF component DCF rather than the routing table's literal BVPS-compounding default for insurers -- see inputs.notes for the full balance-sheet evidence. A literal BVPS-compounding model would understate AIZ badly because book value has been held flat for two decades by a >100%-of-earnings payout policy (buybacks + a 21-year dividend-growth streak), not by weak underlying earnings power.
key_risks_to_valuation: Partner concentration in Global Lifestyle -- loss or repricing of a major carrier/OEM relationship
Global Housing catastrophe and reserve-development volatility, flagged as increasing with climate change
Secular erosion of device-protection attach rates as smartphone replacement cycles lengthen and devices become more durable
Competitive intensity from privately-held Asurion (larger scale in mobile protection) and InsurTech entrants
Model-choice risk: if AIZ's claims tail lengthens or reserve volatility increases materially, the owner-FCF treatment used here would need to revert toward a book-value/reserve-adequacy framing

inputs.wacc_rationale: US large-cap specialty insurer/protection distributor, moderate stable leverage (net debt/owner-FCF ~0.3x), unsecured senior debt costing ~5% (InterestExpenseDebt $109.7M / $2,208M FY2025 balance); built from a ~4.2% 10yr UST + ~4.3pp levered equity risk premium for a mid-beta financial-services name; base 8.5%
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- no disclosed lease liability line comparable in size to debt; ignored
inputs.nci_treatment: not applicable -- no material NCI disclosed
inputs.notes: MODEL DEVIATION FROM THE LITERAL ROUTING TABLE, DOCUMENTED HERE: SKILL.md routes 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book' to BVPS-compounding x exit P/B, and owner-fcf.md explicitly excludes insurers on the grounds that 'an insurer's OCF is noise.' That premise does not hold for AIZ. Balance-sheet evidence: claims reserve liability is only $2.1B against $36.3B total assets (FY2025 10-K, us-gaap:LiabilityForClaimsAndClaimsAdjustmentExpense) -- this is NOT a long-tail P&C/reinsurance float compounder like Fairfax (whose OCF swung -$4.4bn to +$6.6bn on bond mark-to-market). AIZ's liabilities are short-duration unearned premium ($20.9B UPR) matched by deferred acquisition cost assets ($10.2B DAC) from mobile device protection, extended warranties and lender-placed insurance -- fee/premium income on short claim-tail products, closer economically to a fee-based distribution business than an investment-float insurer. Evidence this is the right call, not noise: owner FCF FY2022-2025 is $328.5M -> $856.3M -> $1,016.1M -> $1,498.9M, a coherent growing series tracking revenue and EBITDA-margin expansion, not investment-portfolio noise. Separately, AIZ's book value has been FLAT for two decades (FY2006 equity $3.83B -> FY2025 $5.87B, a 2.3%/yr CAGR despite ~$9bn+ of cumulative net income over the period) because the company returns >100% of earnings most years via buybacks (avg ~$400-500M/yr) plus a 21-year dividend-growth streak on top -- a BVPS-compounding model applied literally would badly understate value because the exit-year book value never reflects the cash already paid out. Routed instead to owner-FCF DCF, treating AIZ as an asset-light fee/premium operating company. Capex is real but small (~1.8-1.9% of revenue, $202-236M/yr, us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment) -- confirms this is not a balance-sheet-heavy insurer. TotalDebt in the Metrics CSV is NULL for all periods (an export gap); verified directly via SEC XBRL us-gaap:UnsecuredDebt = $2,208.1M at 2026-06-30 (matches the pre-2020 us-gaap:LongTermDebt/UnsecuredDebt continuity of $2.0-2.3B since the FY2018 debt issuance); recommend backfilling core_metrics.total_debt from this source. FIX APPLIED (sanity_check.py exit 3, implied P/B 3.39x vs 1.5x-of-10yr-max threshold 3.26x): last_fcf mid-cycled from the FY2025 peak owner-FCF ($1,498.9M, 11.7% margin, OCF/NI conversion >2x) to the FY2023-2025 3yr average owner-FCF margin (9.3%) applied to FY2025 revenue -> $1,193.4M. Base-case EBITDA margin path re-anchored to start from a normalized ~10.9% (FY2023-2025 average EBITDA margin) rather than jumping from the FY2025 peak of 11.3%, still ramping to the same 12.2% mature level over the 10yr horizon.

bear.narrative: A major carrier or OEM partner renegotiates, insources, or is lost -- Global Lifestyle's partner-concentration risk materializes and low-double-digit growth does not scale as guided. Longer smartphone replacement cycles and more durable devices continue eroding device-protection attach rates and claims economics secularly. Global Housing sees a heavier catastrophe year and further adverse reserve development beyond the guided $71M headwind (climate-change-driven volatility flagged explicitly in the risk factors). Competitive pricing pressure from Asurion's scale and InsurTech entrants (Lemonade in renters) compresses margin toward 10%. Buybacks slow as capital is redirected to reserve strengthening.

base.narrative: Global Lifestyle continues scaling recently won/expanded mobile carrier and device-OEM partnerships (low-double-digit segment growth per FY2026 guidance), with trade-in/upgrade programs deepening the ecosystem; Global Housing grows modestly with normal catastrophe/reserve-development noise (the ~$71M FY2026 unfavorable reserve headwind is absorbed, not extrapolated). Revenue growth decelerates from ~8.5% toward a 3% terminal rate as the mobile-protection partnership wins mature. EBITDA margin continues the FY2023-2025 expansion trend (10.0% -> 10.6% -> 11.3%) toward a mature ~12.2%, reflecting AI-enabled claims/service automation and scale economics, then holds flat. Cash tax rate holds near the FY2025 actual (25%) -- no shelter or one-off benefit to unwind. Working capital captures a modest 10% of revenue growth, reflecting UPR (unearned premium reserve) build from a growing insured/enrolled base, partly offset by matching DAC growth.

bull.narrative: New and expanded carrier/OEM partnerships scale faster and stickier than guided, sustaining low-double-digit-plus Global Lifestyle growth for longer; cross-sell of bundled vehicle+mobile protection and international (LatAm/Europe/APAC) Connected Living expansion add a second growth leg. Global Housing avoids major catastrophe years and reserve development turns favorable. Operating leverage and AI-driven claims automation push EBITDA margin further, toward 13.2%. Accelerated buybacks ($300-350M/yr trending to the upper end) compound per-share value on top of the operating growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default shaded slightly toward bear (20% vs the 15% default) given genuine partner-concentration risk in Global Lifestyle (a small number of large carrier/OEM relationships) and explicit catastrophe/climate-change risk in Global Housing flagged in the FY2026 guidance itself (~$71M unfavorable reserve-development headwind already embedded). Bull held at 30% (below the 35% default) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously -- sustained low-double-digit Lifestyle growth AND margin expansion AND a benign catastrophe environment -- rather than one dominant lever.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
